newsitem.title: USA: Four drug makers to pay $12 million in AIDS case.
newsitem.headline: Four drug makers to pay $12 million in AIDS case.

text.p: Four drug makers who have been sued by AIDS-infected hemophiliacs over their blood products have agreed to pay the federal government $12 million to reimburse several health care insurance programs, the U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday.

It said Bayer AG will pay 45 percent of the total; Armour Pharmaceuticals, a division of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc, and a Baxter International Inc unit, each will pay 20 percent; and Alpha Therapeutic Corp, a division of Japan's Green Cross Corp, will pay 15 percent.
From 1978 through 1985, the four companies provided blood products that may have resulted in patients acquiring the virus that causes AIDS, department officials said.
They said individuals who became infected with the virus were in many instances entitled to have federal programs defray their health care costs.

Under the agreement, each member of the class-action lawsuit who signs a separate settlement with the companies entitling them to $100,000 would agree not to pursue any claims against the government, the officials said.
The proposed settlement, which was signed April 30 and announced by the department late Monday, still must be approved by a federal judge in Chicago.

The firms have proposed settling the class-action suit by the hemophiliacs. An attorney told a court hearing in Chicago in November that about 6,200 of the class members, or 95 percent of the total, have approved a $640 million settlement.
The judge has given tentative approval to that settlement.
